verdict_rationale: The two frozen anchors, the pinned and deterministic LPIPS/FloLPIPS scorer and the stated gap-closing formula match the prompt. The task still carries pilot-stage defects. One late or failed request zeroes the run, and an enforced 300 s per-request cap is labelled a debugging limit. The self-check never tests the held-out frame size. 270 correlated intervals give several points of noise, and the GIMM ceiling is nearly reached, compressing the top.
floor: Measured. 0 is 'permitted-standalone-RAFT-deterministic-synthesis': torchvision RAFT-large C_T_SKHT_V2 flow with uniform splatting, no task-time training, on the same 270 intervals (calibration.json:31; pipeline/flow_baseline_results.json). This is a sensible, permitted, training-free baseline that an agent can rebuild in hours. Anything at or below it clips to 0, so a broken model and a plain linear blend both read 0. The baseline's own code (baseline.py, server.py) is listed by hash but is not in the repo.
ceiling: Measured. 1 is GIMM-VFI-R-P, a specialist checkpoint that the task forbids, run on the same 270 intervals (calibration.json:48; anchor_calibration_results.json:29-30 'target_is_permitted_initialization': false, 'permitted_50_dollar_trained_target_demonstrated': false). Each component is clipped at 1. Top trials reach 91-93, so the ceiling nearly binds, and the top is compressed (no per-factor breakdown is published). The anchors changed once: GIMM 'scored exactly 0 on that historical scale; it scores 1 on the current scale' (pipeline/BASELINE.md:35).
usable_range: observed 0-93.2 of 0-100 (Sonnet $200 93.2, Astra $50 91.2, Opus $10 91.1); 13 of 57 trials score 0 (4 of them review fails)
feasible_at_10: yes: Opus 91.1 for $8.10 of 4090 time, Sol 87.8 and Sonnet 86.0 at $10. RAFT plus a refinement U-Net trained on public video train splits gets most of the way.
budget_scaling: Little to none. Opus 91.1/86.7/87.8, Astra 85.3/91.2/84.6, Fable 78.5/81.8/58.2. With the ceiling almost reached at $10 and an SE of a few points, more money mostly adds variance.
selfcheck_fidelity: Good on the request path and the factor mix, weaker on size. The self-check builds a cold pass of public intervals at the evaluation's shape, with factors interleaved, and projects the 2,250 s pass from a sample (verifier.py:183-192, 314-365). It adds frame sizes made by rotating and enlarging the public 384x720 examples: 720x384 and 1081x577 (verifier.py:155-163). The SNU-FILM held-out footage is mostly 1280x720, which the self-check never sends. Per-shape setup or memory at the real size is untested, and the per-request 300 s cap is enforced only in grading.
judge: None in the metric. LPIPS-Alex v0.1 and PWC-Net FloLPIPS are hash-locked, in FP32 with TF32 off and cudnn deterministic (vfi_metrics.py:264-268), so scoring is deterministic. Compliance is gated by the global Claude Opus 5.5 reviewer.
neutrality: The held-out set is SNU-FILM-arb, the protocol of the GIMM-VFI paper whose model sets the ceiling. It is not named to agents. The review rule explicitly forbids its GoPro/YouTube test footage under any name (review.py:56-58), which an agent can only honour by guessing the benchmark. The public examples (one portrait 384x720 clip) hide the held-out resolution. Agents who know the VFI literature (softmax splatting, SNU-FILM conventions) gain, which is arguably skill. No vendor-specific judge.
reference_solution: solution/ is the stdlib smoke fixture. Its /interpolate returns 'blank RGB or nearest PNG' (solution/server.py:102), which would score 0 and fail the 'learned_frame_generation' review check. Solvability is shown by the anchors: the RAFT baseline sits at 0 by construction. The trials show that permitted systems reach about 0.9.

issues.finding: Grading enforces a 300 s per-request timeout, min(300 s, remaining pass time), and any late, failed or malformed request zeroes the whole run with no retries. The contract calls the 300 s figure an 'adjustable debugging limit, not a benchmark speed requirement'. DeepSeek $50 scored 0 on 'Sequence request exceeded its deadline' after a self-check had projected 136 s for the pass.

tests/task/task.yaml:80-81 'these are adjustable debugging limits, not benchmark speed requirements'

issues.affects: Any model with a slow first request or a per-shape stall, toward 0; observed DeepSeek $50

issues.finding: The self-check never sends the held-out frame size. Its extra sizes come from the 384x720 public clip (720x384 and 1081x577), while the SNU-FILM held-out footage is mostly 1280x720. Per-shape compiles, memory and per-pixel time at the graded size are therefore untested before grading.
issues.affects: Servers tuned to the public size; suspected link to DeepSeek $50's zero

issues.finding: There are only 90 intervals per factor, subsampled from the 309 available for speed. Intervals come from overlapping SNU-FILM rows within a few recordings, so they are not independent. The estimated SE of the score, from a paired difference against the anchors, is about 3-5 points. That is enough to swap the Opus/Astra lead at every wallet (margins 3.2-5.8). Using all 927 intervals would cut it by about 1.8x.
evidence: tests/task/pipeline/BASELINE.md:80-88 'one H100 and 270 complete intervals ... The HF payload retains the full set'
tests/task/pipeline/BASELINE.md:101-102 'The smaller sample has greater statistical uncertainty'

issues.finding: The ceiling is a forbidden specialist model, and no permitted system had shown it was reachable when the anchors were frozen. In the event, trials reach 91-93, so the ceiling nearly binds. Per-component clipping at 1 hides any lead beyond GIMM on easy factors and compresses the top.
issues.affects: Top entries (Opus, Astra, Sonnet), compressed together

issues.finding: The public split does not match the documented design. The upload is split 'per interval, and recording groups are shared across the split', against the group-wise split in the pipeline README. The 3 public intervals are a single portrait 384x720 clip, unlike the held-out footage. Tuning on them misled at least one agent (Fable $200: at or below target LPIPS on public, 58.2 on held-out).
evidence: tests/task/pipeline/BASELINE.md:279-282 'The uploaded split is per interval, and recording groups are shared across the split'
tests/task/pipeline/README.md:98-99 '20% of original recording groups for public validation'
issues.affects: Agents that select inference settings on the public examples, downward

issues.finding: The task was graded while still marked a pilot whose release checks are unfinished. Media rights are also unresolved, though the held-out frames sit in a public HF dataset.
evidence: tests/task/pipeline/BASELINE.md:8-9 'Release still requires pretrained scorer parity, corruption controls, and validation of the serving-speed gate'
issues.affects: Benchmark validity overall; no model-specific direction

issues.finding: The agent is not told that the held-out set is SNU-FILM. The review nonetheless rejects use of 'their underlying GoPro/YouTube test footage under another name'. The general test-split rule covers GoPro test; YouTube clips have no named split an agent could avoid.
evidence: tests/task/review.py:56-58 'SNU-FILM, SNU-FILM-arb and SNU-FILM-entire are evaluation data; using their underlying GoPro/YouTube test footage under another name is still excluded'
issues.affects: None observed (no trial used SNU-FILM or GoPro test)
